milestone.title: Theme system follow-up — per-component accent roles (focus_ring + surface_1 + surface_2)

intent.outcome: Extend the Palette struct with three new roles (focus_ring, surface_1, surface_2) so renderers can use them in addition to the 6 base roles. Every palette in theme.rs (latte, frappe, macchiato, mocha, dracula, alucard + monochrome) gets matching colors picked from the official spec. The milestones tab, picker, Settings header, and While-Executing takeover use the new roles for visual layering — currently everything maps to accent / foreground / dim and gets visually loud.

problem.description: After M243 ships the live-apply picker, raul will have a working theme system with 6 base semantic colors. But the renderer set currently collapses every visual layer onto accent / foreground / dim: the floating picker backdrop, the sidebar tab strip, the Activity-tab filter chip, the milestone detail's per-AC row, the while-executing topo strip. This makes the TUI visually loud — there are no quiet layers. Adding focus_ring (a quiet contrast color for the focused chip / selected-row overlay), surface_1 (a quiet panel background for sidebars / picker surfaces), and surface_2 (a slightly brighter panel background for nested layers like the Activity tab inside the Progress tab) gives renderers a 9-role color vocabulary. Without this, picking accent-only keeps the surface flat, and themes that lean on neutral palettes (Dracula, Alucard) under-deliver visually vs. what's in the official color docs.

in_scope: Extend crates/raul/src/theme.rs::Palette with three new fields: focus_ring (used for selected-row outlines, focused-key chips, focused-button borders; named in the same color-spec role style as accent), surface_1 (a quiet panel background for sidebars, picker surfaces, and right-rail regions), surface_2 (a slightly brighter panel background for nested layers / hover states / disabled buttons). All three are populated per-palette: Mocha picks Mauve / Mantle / Surface0, Frappe picks its Mauve / Mantle / Surface0, Dracula picks Purple / Current Line / Selection, Alucard the same palette's adjusted-for-light tone, Latte picks Mauve / Crust / Mantle.

Update every renderer that uses palette.* to also expose the new colors; specifically: crates/raul/src/tui/render/lane_lists.rs (milestone table row hover / selected highlights, the picker surface bg, the dropdown surface), crates/raul/src/tui/render/dashboard_view.rs (lane-tab focus state), crates/raul/src/tui/render/overlays.rs (modal-backdrop tint), crates/raul/src/tui/render/board.rs (selected-cell ring), crates/raul/src/tui/render/milestone_detail.rs (per-AC row focus overlay), crates/raul/src/tui/render/chrome.rs (header / footer bg), crates/raul/src/tui/path_view.rs (lane ↔ row connector), crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings/theme_picker.rs (focused-row outline and selection chip)
Extend the synthetic status preview row (built in M243 WP2 step S2.1) to render with the new roles when they exist (focus_ring on 'selected', surface_1 behind the row).
Add a unit test in crates/raul/src/tui/palette.rs that asserts each palette's new three colors match the spec (snapshot-style), so a future palette addition fails CI if it skips the new fields.
Document the new roles in docs/raul/settings.md or a new docs/raul/theme-roles.md with a table: which renderer uses which role for what.
Add CSS-style role comments in crates/raul/src/theme.rs (e.g., on the focus_ring field: 'used for selected-row outlines in lists; bright but quiet so it doesn't compete with accent').
out_of_scope: Auto-detection of terminal capability (COLORFTERM / $TERM) and suggesting monochrome: deferred to a follow-up.
Custom user palettes (~/.config/raul/themes/*.toml): per M243 T-4 user direction, not planned.
Light/dark variants beyond what already exists (Latte, Alucard are the light variants).
Per-renderer CSS-like stylesheets or a separate theme override file format: out of scope; this milestone only adds the Palette fields and update renderers to use them.
Round-tripping the existing 6 themes — those are already correct per the audit; M244 only ADDS new colors and updates renderers.

acceptance_criteria.description: Palette struct has the three new fields focus_ring, surface_1, surface_2, all populated for each of the 6 named palettes (latte, frappe, macchiato, mocha, dracula, alucard) — values derived from each palette's official spec.
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo test -p raul theme_palette_new_fields; cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/palette_has_focus_ring|palette_has_surface_1|palette_has_surface_2/)'

acceptance_criteria.description: Every renderer in scope consumes at least one of the new roles where relevant: lane_lists.rs, dashboard_view.rs, overlays.rs, board.rs, milestone_detail.rs, chrome.rs, path_view.rs, settings/theme_picker.rs.
acceptance_criteria.verification: rg -n 'palette\.(focus_ring|surface_1|surface_2)' crates/raul/src/tui/render 2>&1 must return at least 6 hits; cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/renderer_uses_new_palette_roles/)'

acceptance_criteria.description: The synthetic status preview row in crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings/theme_picker.rs renders the focused/selected row using palette.focus_ring (border) and palette.surface_1 (background); non-focused rows use foreground / dim only.
A unit test asserts that adding a 7th palette without populating the new fields fails compile (via a const-fn assertion or const_assert). This prevents a future palette regression.

Switching themes in the Settings lane (M243 picker) reflects the new roles throughout the TUI live: focused chips in the picker change outline color, panel backgrounds in the sidebar shift tone, and the milestone detail's per-AC row hover state uses the focus_ring color.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual verification + cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/theme_picker_render_with_new_roles/)'

acceptance_criteria.description: make lint + make test + make consumer-surface-lint + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings remain green.
acceptance_criteria.verification: make lint && make test && make consumer-surface-lint
